title: Change to quotient coefficients for an annihilated sheaf
statement: Let Λ be a commutative ring, n a natural number, q an integer, and Y --e→ T, Y --h→ X, T --g→ S, X --p→ S a cartesian square [sbc-def-base-change-square], with g quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Assume BC(p,Λ/(n),q): the degree-q base-change map is invertible in every such base-change square for every sheaf of Λ/(n)-modules. For any sheaf F of Λ-modules on T_et with n times its identity zero, its degree-q base-change map [sbc-def-base-change-map] is an isomorphism.

source.place: Module docstring: Change of rings; docstring of Etale.isIso_baseChangeHomologyMap_of_nsmul_eq_zero

proof.text: Set R=Λ/(n) and G=Hom_Λ(R,F), the sheaf coextension of scalars. The counit Res G→F is an isomorphism. Sectionwise it is evaluation at 1. ModuleCat.mono_coextendQuotientShortComplex_f gives its injectivity. ModuleCat.exact_coextendQuotientShortComplex says its image is the kernel of multiplication by n; n times the identity of F is zero, so this kernel is all of F. These pointwise isomorphisms are a sheaf isomorphism. The helper isIso_quotientCounit proves this in Lean.

The hypothesis BC(p,R,q), unfolded, makes the base-change map of G over R an isomorphism. Restriction of scalars preserves this isomorphism. Apply the coefficient comparison [lem-sbc-base-change-restrict-scalars-arrow] to obtain that the base-change map of Res G over Λ is an isomorphism.

Naturality of the base-change map for the counit c:Res G→F expresses its value at F as (source.map c) inverse, followed by its value at Res G, followed by target.map c. All three factors are isomorphisms, hence so is their composite. This is the original theorem with unchanged hypotheses, including n=0 and n=1.
